details: A peace agreement or framework between the United States and Iran has been signed, leading to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. While the initial news in mid-June prompted a risk-on sentiment in broader financial markets and a brief rise in Bitcoin, crypto markets quickly became cautious. Investors are now weighing the de-escalation of Middle East tensions against hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve and broader macroeconomic conditions. The deal aims to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons and includes a commitment to toll-free passage through the Strait of Hormuz, a key global energy route.
title: US-Iran Peace Deal Signed, Market Response Mixed

details: Despite the US-Iran agreement, Bitcoin and other major cryptocurrencies have seen declines following hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve. The Fed kept interest rates unchanged at its June meeting but indicated that an increasing number of policymakers are considering a rate hike later in 2026 due to inflation risks. This stance has rattled speculative assets, including cryptocurrencies, with investors reducing exposure to risk assets amidst monetary policy uncertainty.
title: Federal Reserve Hawkish Stance Weighs on Crypto

details: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is reportedly preparing a new policy that would permit crypto companies to offer blockchain-based tokenized stock trading. This development, if implemented, could significantly impact the structure of traditional US equity markets by allowing crypto-native platforms to offer stock exposure. The proposal aims for a lighter-touch regulatory approach, enabling experimentation with new digital asset business models, although it has already drawn opposition from established financial market participants like Citadel Securities and SIFMA over concerns of diverting liquidity and regulatory arbitrage risks.
title: SEC Reportedly Preparing to Greenlight Tokenized Stock Trading

details: The US Department of the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and major federal banking regulators have jointly proposed a rule requiring permitted payment stablecoin issuers to establish formal customer identification programs. Under this proposal, stablecoin issuers would be officially classified as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act, mandating rigorous anti-money laundering (AML) and identity verification procedures. This includes collecting specific customer data and establishing risk-based protocols to verify identities.
title: US Regulators Propose Stablecoin Customer Verification Rules
